passage:
I'm Aparna, and I was in the back room of Ramesh's family's hardware shop when his uncle told him, again, "Be satisfied. We have a roof and a shop. Why this design college nonsense?" Ramesh, who is twenty, looked at the floor and said, "I am grateful, Chacha." The uncle said, "Then act like it."
Ramesh's ears went red. I can't know exactly what he felt, but he went out and sat on the loading step with a sketchbook for a long time. Later he said to me, "I'm not saying the shop is small. I just want to learn design too."
His uncle glanced over from the counter, saw the sketchbook, and turned away.

qa.q: What did Ramesh's uncle say he should be?
qa.a: His uncle told him to be satisfied.

qa.q: What was Ramesh feeling when the uncle said "Then act like it"?
qa.a: Ramesh felt hurt and misunderstood, with red ears and a long silence on the loading step, since his gratitude was treated as if it were absent.

qa.q: What could Ramesh say to his uncle to show gratitude and ambition together?
qa.a: Ramesh could say he is thankful for the shop and also wants to learn design, maybe offering to help at the shop while studying.

qa.q: How might the uncle see Ramesh's interest in design?
qa.a: The uncle may see it as ingratitude or as leaving the family, since he called it nonsense and turned away. He may also worry about the family's security.

grounding: A young person who wants a bigger life is told to be satisfied; wanting more can coexist with gratitude.

passage:
Friday. At dinner Rukmini mentioned a scholarship for studying abroad. Her father put down his spoon. "We have a home, food, each other. Why aren't you satisfied?" She said nothing more.
Saturday. On the terrace she told Zainab, "It's like wanting more means I'm ungrateful."
"Are you?"
"No. I'm grateful every single day."
Wednesday. Rukmini found her father alone with the newspaper. "Papa, I'm grateful for this house. And I still want to try for the scholarship. Both are true."
He was silent for a while. "I hadn't thought of it that way," he said. He didn't say yes. But he moved the newspaper so she could sit beside him.

qa.q: Which day did Rukmini tell Zainab on the terrace?
qa.a: Rukmini told Zainab on Saturday.

qa.q: What was Rukmini feeling on the terrace when she said wanting more felt like being ungrateful?
qa.a: Rukmini felt hurt and confused, worried that her ambition would be read as a lack of thanks.

qa.q: What did Rukmini do on Wednesday that opened the conversation?
qa.a: Rukmini told her father she was grateful for the house and still wanted to try, calling both true. That let him hear her ambition without feeling rejected.

qa.q: How might Rukmini's father have felt when she spoke on Wednesday?
qa.a: He was probably surprised and thoughtful, since he said he hadn't thought of it that way. Moving the newspaper suggests he was making room for her.

grounding: A young person who wants a bigger life is told to be satisfied with what the family has; wanting more coexists with gratitude.

passage:
Dear Lokesh dada,

I know Papa talked to you after dinner. I'm writing because when I speak, it comes out wrong.

I applied to the film school in Pune. I didn't tell anyone because I knew what Papa would say: "We have the shop, we have a roof, why isn't that enough?" And he did say it. He called me ungrateful.

But dada, I am grateful. I know Papa worked seventeen-hour days to build that shop. I've worked there every summer since I was twelve, and I'm proud of it.

I just want to try something bigger. Wanting more doesn't mean I think what we have is small.

Could you help me talk to him? He listens to you.

Your brother,
Arnab

qa.q: Where is the film school Arnab applied to?
qa.a: In Pune.

qa.q: How did Arnab feel when Papa called him ungrateful?
qa.a: Arnab felt hurt and misunderstood, because he is truly grateful and proud of the shop but still wants something bigger.

qa.q: How could Lokesh dada help Arnab and Papa?
qa.a: He could help Arnab explain calmly that he respects the shop and Papa's work, and that wanting a bigger life isn't a rejection.

qa.q: How might Papa see Arnab's application?
qa.a: Papa may see it as ingratitude toward the life he built, and may also be afraid of Arnab leaving.

grounding: Shows a young person told to be satisfied with what the family has, who wants more while remaining grateful.

passage:
"Shalini, you asked why I've been so quiet at home. It's me, Yusuf, talking too much again.
So I got into a master's programme in Hyderabad. Full scholarship. I was over the moon. I told Ammi and Abbu, and Ammi said, 'Why do you always want more? We have a good life here. Be thankful.'
And I sat there feeling like a thief, like wanting more was stealing from them.
But I am thankful. I know Abbu took the night bus to Bareilly for years so we could study. That's exactly why I want to go. Their work gave me a bigger world. I want to walk into it.
I think 'be content' sometimes means 'don't leave us.' I get that. I'm still going. I just want them to see it's gratitude too."

qa.q: Where did Yusuf get into a master's programme?
qa.a: In Hyderabad.

qa.q: What was Yusuf feeling when Ammi said 'Be thankful'?
qa.a: Yusuf felt guilty, like a thief, as if wanting more was stealing from the family.

qa.q: What small step could Yusuf take with Ammi and Abbu?
qa.a: Yusuf could tell them directly that the dream grows from their sacrifice, maybe by thanking Abbu for those night-bus years.

qa.q: Why might Ammi have said 'Why do you always want more?'
qa.a: She may have been afraid of Yusuf leaving home, and the call for contentment might really mean 'don't leave us'.

grounding: Shows a young person told to be content with the family's life who realises that ambition and gratitude can coexist.

passage:
March: Tanuja told her father at dinner that she wanted to train as a pilot. Her father, Lokesh, put down his roti. "We have a good life in Kanpur. Your job at the bank is stable. Why can't you be satisfied?" Tanuja went to her room feeling ungrateful and small.
April: She wrote him a list: what she loved about home, and what she wanted to try. She left it on his desk. He didn't mention it, but she saw he'd kept it.
June: Tanuja found her father on the balcony, reading about the flight school's open day. "I thought 'be content' was the right thing to say," he said slowly. "Maybe I was just scared." Tanuja sat next to him. "I'm grateful, Papa. And I still want to fly." He nodded. "Then we'll go to the open day together."

qa.q: What job did Tanuja have?
qa.a: Her job at the bank.

qa.q: How did Tanuja feel after the March dinner?
qa.a: She felt ungrateful and small, as if wanting more was wrong.

qa.q: What small step helped her father understand?
qa.a: Tanuja's list of what she loved about home and what she wanted to try, which showed her gratitude and her dream side by side.

qa.q: How did Lokesh's view change by June?
qa.a: He realised his call for contentment came from fear, and decided to go to the open day with her.

grounding: Shows a young person told to be satisfied with what the family has, whose ambition turns out to coexist with gratitude.

passage: Suraj, you think I don't understand why you want to go to Bengaluru? Listen. When I was nineteen I wanted to train as a teacher in the town. My father said, "We have land, we have food, a good match is coming. Why do you want more? Be thankful." I was thankful, kanna. I loved our fields. But I also wanted more, and he made me feel those two things could not live in one heart. For a year I didn't mention it. Then my mother sat with him one night and said, "She is not rejecting us. She is asking to grow from us." He was quiet a long time. The next June he took me to the training college himself. So go. Wanting more is not the same as being ungrateful. Your Rukmini Paati knows.

qa.q: What did Rukmini want to train as when she was nineteen?
qa.a: She wanted to train as a teacher in the town.

qa.q: How did young Rukmini feel when her father told her to be thankful?
qa.a: She felt torn and guilty, loving the fields yet wanting more, as if the two could not live in one heart.

qa.q: What turned things around in the story, and why did it work?
qa.a: Her mother telling him that Rukmini was asking to grow from them, not rejecting them, which let him see ambition and gratitude together.

qa.q: How might Rukmini's father have seen her wish at first?
qa.a: He probably saw it as ingratitude and felt hurt, since land, food and a good match seemed like enough.

grounding: Shows a young woman told to be satisfied with what the family has, and her ambition later accepted as compatible with gratitude.
